newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Goodale sets Red River flood zone funds.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Goodale sets Red River flood zone funds.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale on Wednesday set aside funds for farmers in the Red River Valley's flood zone and may top up the compensation later this month, an Agriculture Canada statement said.

"In light of Manitoba's decision to extend seeding deadlines for the purposes of its crop insurance program, Agriculture Canada will reassess the need for further assistance toward the end of June," Goodale said.
Manitoba extended its crop insurance deadline by five days to mid-June after 600,000 acres of Red River Valley farmland was submerged in April to May by the worst flood in 145 years.

Goodale, who was widely expected to be appointed to the energy and mines ministry later Wednesday when the newly re-elected Liberal Party swears in its cabinet, announced the Crop Restoration Program.
The program sets aside C$10 an acre to defray the cost of custom seeding of as many acres as possible before the cut off dates under Manitoba's revised crop insurance program.
It also allocates C$500,000 to ensure machines, seed, fertilizer and other supplies are available to assist in seeding.
